subject: Career
title: Servant Leadership: Power Through Service
description: A micro-lesson that makes Servant Leadership: Power Through Service usable.

hook.text: The CEO carries her own coffee. She answers junior employees' questions. Her power grows because she doesn't hoard it.

buildup.text: Robert Greenleaf coined 'servant leadership' in 1970: leaders serve first, lead second.

discovery.text: Research shows servant-led teams have 6% higher performance and 50% higher retention.

twist.text: Servant leadership is sometimes mistaken for weakness. But earning loyalty through service is the strongest power base.

climax.text: Ask: 'What do you need to succeed?' Then deliver. Your team's success becomes your power.

punchline.text: The most powerful leaders make everyone around them more powerful.

quiz.question: What is servant leadership?
options: Leaders serve first and lead second, growing power through service
Leaders serve coffee to their team

details.summary: Servant leadership inverts the traditional power hierarchy by positioning the leader's primary role as serving their team's needs. This approach builds deep loyalty, trust, and performance by removing obstacles and empowering others to do their best work.
details.whyItMatters: Servant leadership builds the most durable form of power because it is based on genuine reciprocity. Teams under servant leaders consistently outperform those led by authority-driven managers.
takeaways: Servant leaders prioritize removing obstacles for their team
This approach builds referent power through genuine respect
Servant leadership does not mean avoiding difficult decisions

faq.question: Is servant leadership effective in competitive corporate environments?
faq.answer: Yes. Companies like Southwest Airlines and Costco have demonstrated that servant leadership produces strong financial results alongside high employee satisfaction. The style works in competitive environments precisely because it generates loyalty and discretionary effort.

faq.question: How do servant leaders handle situations that require tough decisions?
faq.answer: Servant leaders still make difficult decisions, including terminations and budget cuts. The difference is they communicate with empathy, explain the reasoning transparently, and ensure affected individuals are treated with dignity throughout the process.
